subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw add a core temp artifact provenance registry and runtime-critical temp path guardrails, and if so which storage and cleanup authority owns them?
rationale: The request crosses storage model, cleanup authority, agent/tool API shape, doctor checks, runtime/bootstrap validation, and core-versus-plugin boundary; automation cannot safely choose that product shape.

options.title: Core guardrails plus provenance seam
options.body: Core would own runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific classifications stay in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Core would own temp artifact classes, registry, cleanup/janitor behavior, and durable routing policy for all first-class OpenClaw-created temp artifacts.

options.title: Narrow runtime-path checks only
options.body: Core would implement warning/fail checks for runtime-critical temp-backed paths and defer artifact lifecycle provenance to separate plugin/API discussion.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus provenance seam
recommendation.body: Core would own runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific classifications stay in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily product boundary plus storage policy, and steipete has the strongest current-main and related-decision trail for those surfaces.
